text:
mina: kicking off carrack18b-int4 canary this morning. seeing a small but consistent drop on code-completion benchmarks vs fp16 baseline. also some sporadic OOMs under synth burst tests. starting thread to triage.
raj: can you share numbers and infra?
mina: running on 48GB A100 canary pool, 8 hosts. sample workload is code-complete (avg prompt len 120 tokens, typical completion 30-200 tokens).
lee: describe the OOM pattern? single big alloc or fragmentation?
mina: logs show fragmentation + sudden large allocation for KV when longer completions hit. sample below.
```
[2025-01-12T14:12:03Z] kv_alloc: current_frag_ratio=0.34
[2025-01-12T14:12:03Z] prefetch: window=3 segments=6
[2025-01-12T14:12:03Z] cuda: malloc failed requested=384MB free=120MB
[2025-01-12T14:12:03Z] OOM at kv_alloc -> evict scheduled -> fallback to fp16
```
raj: prefetch_window=3 is aggressive for code workloads with many short completions. That plus int4 alignment can amplify fragmentation.
perf-bot: baseline vs canary quickbench: exact-match code tests -1.8%, compilation-syntax false positive +0.9%, p95 latency +12%, mem_frag_index 0.31, kv_evictions 2.2/min
lee: -1.8% is worrying for code customers. Did quant eval run with instruction-tuning test set?
mina: yes we ran the code-quality suite; regressions concentrated on long-tail token-level accuracy (indentation, closing brackets). suspected causes: quantization noise + reduced max_new_tokens default allowing longer chains to misalign.
raj: short-term mitigations:
- reduce prefetch_window to 1
- set model-catalog default_max_new_tokens for carrack18b-int4 -> 128
- enable kv_trim_on_idle and more aggressive compaction
- lower max_batch_tokens to 2048 for canary hosts
lee: also recommend soft rollback mapping to carrack18b-fp16 with priority routing for code endpoints.
mina: testing a tuning patch now; applying these changes to one host and running the code suite A/B.
perf-bot: quick A/B (host patch applied): p95 latency -5% vs canary, mem_frag_index -> 0.11, kv_evictions 0.4/min, code exact-match delta -0.3% (improved but still slightly worse than fp16).
raj: improvements look good. -0.3% may be acceptable depending on customer SLAs. What's root cause hypothesis?
lee: two-fold: int4 quantization slightly reduces token prediction confidence on rare tokens (braces/indentation), and prefetching + large batch tokens cause fragmentation spikes that lead to fallbacks and tail latency which hurts sequence coherency.
mina: plan:
- promote tuned serving.config (prefetch_window=1, max_batch_tokens=2048, eviction_threshold_ms=500, max_new_tokens=128) to canary 10% for 4h
- run full code regression eval at 4h mark; if exact-match delta <= -0.5% proceed to 50%
- create model-catalog patch to set default_max_new_tokens=128 for int4 variant and document conservative defaults
- schedule nightly compaction during 02:00 UTC low-traffic window
infra-bot: ticket created INF-992 (canary config patch), INF-993 (model-catalog default change), INF-994 (nightly compaction job).
perf-bot: added alerts: kv_evictions > 1/min and mem_frag_index > 0.25 for carrack18b-int4 canary.
raj: also capture per-token logits for a subset of failing QA examples to analyze quant noise. Mina can you attach those to INF-992?
mina: yes will attach. adding a short ablation: try per-layer symmetric quant vs asymmetric on final layers to see effect on code tokens.
lee: good. if regression persists after these, we'll fallback rollout and consider per-task model routing (code->fp16).
mina: running canary now, will update thread after 4h check. thanks all. :computer:
